    Suzanne LaFrance, Mayor
                              Sept 21 2026
                     GBOS Regular Meeting
                              Minutes Final
         7:00 p.m. via Microsoft Teams & Girdwood Community Room

This hybrid meeting is taking place via Microsoft Teams & at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Rd:

The Girdwood Board of Supervisors is subject to the Alaska Open Meetings Act as found in Alaska Statute 44.62.310
and Anchorage Municipal Code1.25 - Public Meetings.
The Girdwood Board of Supervisors operates under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

Call to Order 7:00 p.m.  Kellie Okonek, Co-Chair

Land Acknowledgement: The Girdwood Board of Supervisors acknowledges the indigenous peoples of Alaska, whose land we
reside on. The community of Girdwood, situated between the areas known to be Dena'ina and Alutiiq homeland, respects the people
who were stewards of this land for generations. We commit to the continued stewardship of this land and are grateful to be part of a
wider community that seeks to maintain a sustainable use of Girdwood Valley for present and future peoples.

Roll Call: Jennifer Wingard (JW), Brian Burnett (BB) Amanda Tuttle (AT), Nick Crews (NC), Kellie Okonek (KO)
No Disclosures

Announcements:
    •  GHEC has two vacant positions, to be filled by registered voters in the Girdwood Valley Service Area. To be
       considered for appointment, email gbos@muni.org.
    •  PSAC has one vacant position, to be filled by registered voters in the Girdwood Valley Service Area. To be
       considered for appointment, email GBOS@muni.org
    •  GBOS Non-Profit grant presentation meeting is scheduled for MON Set 28 at 6PM in the Girdwood Community
      Room.
    •  MOA GBOS Quarterly Meeting is scheduled for MON Oct 26 at 4PM at the Girdwood Community Room.
    •  See meeting packet for various items coming up for hearing

Agenda Revisions and Approval:   September 21 2026 GBOS agenda approved  JW/BB        Assent
                             Amendment to add item #7 setback variance  AT/BB         Assent
Minutes Approval:                 August 17 2026 GBOS meeting minutes approved JW/BB      Assent
                                  August 31 2026 GBOS SM minutes approved  JW/AT         Assent
Presentations (10 Min):        AWWU Presentation: Mario Croce, AWWU Plant Manager
                                   Sandy Baker, AWWU Public Outreach Officer
Girdwood Plant just received Peak Performance Award, which they have received for the last 10 years.
Issue brought up at prior meeting with non-compliance over several quarters was an incident that was corrected but
paperwork error kept it on the EPA list. AWWU is working on their Waste Water Master Plan and Facility Master Plan.
Capacity of the plant, both as far as treatment and water is under consideration. Recent increase in homes has not
changed the volume of water/treatment substantially. There are several factors that account for this, including lower
flow and more efficient water systems. Capacity is 600,000 gal/day; use is typically 450,000 gal/day.

           GBOS Meeting Agendas and minutes are available on line: http://www.muni.org/gbos
                                                                                         1

AWWU offers to schedule a tour of the facility for GBOS and invites additional questions at that time.

Consent agenda: None
Reports (5 Min):
1.  Legislative Report – Rep. Ky Holland
    Effort to bring in-person early voting option to Girdwood was not successful but will try again for upcoming
    elections. Waterfall funding has provided $32M to ASD and funds to residents via PFD.
   Ongoing effort to secure natural gas source for future.
   Assembly members – Z. Johnson/Keith McCormick: No report
   Anchorage School Board Liaison – Rachel Blakeslee: No report
   HLBAC Report – Tim Charnon: See meeting packet

2.  Supervisor Reports
   KO: GHEC reviewed RFP for housing study, discussed property tax exemptions and is working on definition of
    Workforce housing
   PSAC: Meeting in October
    Trails: New trails maps complete
   LUC: see meeting minutes
    Fire: EMS Funding request later in the meeting.

3.  Committee updates to GBOS: 3 min each; items not on the agenda but items of interest to the community
   None

4.  Standing Reports: See meeting packet
    Glacier Valley Lodge Airport development: Lease with DOT was signed this summer. Developers had tried to
   amend the lease agreement, but were not successful. Signed lease has 5 year time requirement to complete
   construction of the lodge and facilities. If not completed, the lease agreement expires. There are provisions that
   must be completed before construction: Building permit requires traffic study; FAA requires full NEPA review. MOA
    legal still holds to the idea that a Municipal Land Use Permit is required. This would come up later when closer to
   construction.
   As an unmanned airport, DOT says that the Emergency Response Plan for the airport is a matter to be established
   between the airport Manager (DOT manager for Girdwood is Paul Berthall) and Fire Dept.
    Airport Master Plan is due however was postponed due to budget constraints in 2026. DOT Airports division is
   working through other Master Plan efforts, Girdwood Airport remains on the list for completion.

5.  Service Provider Reports (5 mins each)
         Fire – Chief Weston: 19 calls in August; 36 so far in September, including fire in Whittier
        Police – Chief Achee: New officer in training. Usually an uptick in theft etc in fall.
       Roads/Parks & Rec – Kyle Kelley: see meeting packet
       Anchorage Public Library – Katarina Pavic, Gerrish (Girdwood) Branch Manager: See meeting packet.

PUBLIC COMMENT:    None

OLD BUSINESS:
6.  Agenda Item LUC 2026-04: FCC Delegate from GBOS (Land Use Committee Supervisor)
    Motion:
   GBOS moves to not continue sending delegate to FCC.
    Motion by JW/2nd AT

   Amendment motion:
   Add to motion: If there is a change, GBOS will specifically assign delegate to represent Girdwood.
   Amendment by JW/2nd BB
   Amendment accepted 5-0 in roll call vote

    Revised motion:
   GBOS moves to pull the official Girdwood delegate to FCC. If GBOS choses to assign a delegate in the future, this will take place
     via specific GBOS action.
    Motion approved 3-2 in roll call vote. (BB and NC dissenting)

    Jennifer Wingard, who has served as the official delegate to FCC, is to provide this information to FCC.


                                                                                         2

7.  Case 2026-125 Request for Dimensional Variance Stream Setback 158 Northland Road; ZBEA Hearing Oct 8 2026.
    Item was originally heard in 2024 and GBOS objected at that time. Since then the owner has worked with watershed and other
    municipal departments to meet requirements and has been granted non-conforming use.
    Neighbors just became aware this week of pending action at ZBEA Oct 8 and have collected letters of concern related to
    watershed and stream setback variance.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to send letter of objection to ZBEA, pending formal watershed study and community input.
    Motion by AT, no second. Motion dies

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to request delay to hearing date.
    Motion by AT, no second. Motion dies.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to send a letter to the Appeals board requesting that all comments of neighbors are fully vetted acknowledging
     petitioner’s work.
    Motion by JW/2nd AT
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote

   JW is to write a letter to ZBEA from GBOS.

8. PSAC Request for letters to DOT requesting DOT provide a liaison to attend meetings in Girdwood (Tuttle)
    Nothing to report on this item.

9.  Girdwood Parks Plan: Little Bears and Glacier City Hall buildings (Staff)
    Meeting packet includes structural study performed in 2021. Based on this study, Little Bears building to be demolished in the
     future.

    Alyeska Resort representative states that resort is also removing structures that are out of operational use and offers to
     collaborate.

10. PSAC Vacancy: Received resume late in the day today, confirming interest from this individual. Item will be added to the GBOS
    Special meeting next week.

11. LUC Recommendation for GBOS Resolution of Support to transfer Girdwood Industrial Park lot, HLB Parcel ID 6-057K/Parcel ID
    075-131-18 to MOA Street Maintenance – Girdwood. (Wingard/staff)

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to approve Resolution 2026-09 as presented.
    Motion by JW/2nd AT
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote


12. GBOS Resolution of Support for increase in EMS Funding from Municipality of Anchorage for Girdwood Fire Dept, following 2027
    budget discussions. (Crews)
    Nick and Chief Weston are working on final draft Resolution which will be complete by tomorrow. Requested increase is $106,114,
    matching request already submitted to GFR.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to approve Resolution 2026-10 as discussed. Final language to be shared with GBOS with 24 hour review.
    Motion by NC/2nd JW
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote


13. Request for HLB to share method for communicating information about timeline and requirements for bidders interested in
    Girdwood Industrial Park lot to be disposed via competitive bid. (Wingard/staff)
   HLB has shared their method with Jennifer Wingard. Disposal will need first to be included and approved in the HLB 1 year work
     plan. After that, the land will be appraised, presented as potential for MOA internal use/disposal, and then reviewed at HLBAC.
    Marketing of the land would occur after all of those steps, notification to leaseholders of the GIP, information on HLB website.
   GBOS and GBOS members can also share information about land available for competitive bid.

                                                                                         3

Jennifer and Amanda to discuss further.

14. GBOS consider writing a letter to Department of Environmental Conservation regarding AWWU discharge violations (Tuttle)
    Presentation earlier by AWWU indicates that there are not ongoing discharge violations.
   Amanda remains interested in writing letter to DEC. She requests item stay on the agenda to review letter.

15. GBOS request: MOA release data regarding bed tax accrued in Girdwood. (Crews)
   New registration of STRs is step in providing information on STR bed tax accrued in Girdwood.
    Nick is researching the accrual and amounts of funds received through bed tax as well as how those funds are spent.
    Item to be discussed at the MOA GBOS Quarterly meeting in October.

16. Update on the Road Maintenance contract bid for 2026-27 and beyond, with the award to Western Construction
    Western Construction has won the bid and price increases will need to be incorporated into the budget. See meeting packet for
    itemized costs.

17. Revisit the Girdwood Fire 2026 Budget Revision approval to transfer $24k from the Fire Capital Contribution to the Operating
     contract. We will be seeking a vote from GBOS to reconfirm that they support this transfer.
    Funds were to have been moved in 1Q revisions but did not.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to transfer $24,000 from the Girdwood Fire capital fund to operating budget.
    Motion by NC/2nd JW
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote

18. GBOS Bylaws revisions (Wingard)
    Revisions as discussed previously are presented in the meeting packet. Jennifer and Nick will continue to work on them and
    provide an updated draft for GBOS to review and likely put forward for public review.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to hold a Special Meeting on GBOS Bylaws.
    Motion by JW/2nd AT
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote.

    Special meeting will be polled for once Jennifer and Nick indicate they are ready to proceed. Supervisors are encouraged to bring
     their suggestions for revision to the meeting.

NEW BUSINESS:
19. Discuss agenda topics for October 26 MOA GBOS Quarterly Meeting (Girdwood-based)

    Motion by BB/2nd AT
    Motion carries by assent

    Motion:

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to hear the Girdwood Art Council presentation although the application was received late.
    Motion by BB/2nd NC
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote
